teile.text: In 1923, Walt Disney’s Laugh‑O‑Gram studio went bankrupt, prompting a move to Los Angeles.
teile.szene: An ink-splattered animator in a cluttered 1920s room looks at a foreclosure notice on a wooden desk under dim yellow lighting, medium shot.

teile.text: He signed a $1,500 contract with Margaret Winkler for the Alice Comedies series.
teile.szene: A frustrated man in a dark vest tears a drawing of a rabbit in half inside a cramped office with dusty windows, close-up.

teile.text: In 1927 Disney produced Oswald for Universal, but the rights were retained by Universal after a 1928 dispute.
teile.szene: An artist rapidly sketches a small mouse on paper at night under a single swinging bulb, tight shot with dramatic shadows.

teile.text: Facing that loss, Walt renamed his new mouse character Mickey, a change suggested by his wife.
teile.szene: A vintage film projector spins inside a crowded 1928 theater booth while beams of light cut through dust, wide angle.

teile.text: Steamboat Willie debuted in 1928 and was the first cartoon with synchronized sound, striking an instant hit.
teile.szene: Excited patrons queue outside a vintage theater marquee displaying a classic animated film title, medium shot in sepia tones.

teile.text: The success spurred Mickey’s 1930 licensing, turning Disney into a global merchandise power.
teile.szene: Stacked wooden crates stamped with cartoon characters fill a bustling 1930s warehouse under bright afternoon light, wide shot.

teile.text: The Walt Disney Company began in 1923 after Laugh‑O‑Gram collapsed—now a worldwide empire; like, share, save.
teile.szene: A man in a vintage suit holds up a framed pencil sketch of a mouse, smiling slightly in a warm study, medium portrait shot.

entwurf.beschreibung: Discover how the Walt Disney Company rose from sudden bankruptcy and a stolen character to build a global entertainment empire starting in 1923.
